full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Shamsul Huda, J. : This Rule is directed on an application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of the defendant appellant petitioners against the judgment and decree dated 30.4.1997 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Naogaon in Title Appeal No. 222 of 1993, affirming the judgment and decree dated 21.8.1993 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Naogaon in Other Class Suit No. 125 of 1.991 decreeing the suit. 

2. The facts relevant for the disposal of this Rule in brief are that, the opposite parties being plaintiffs instituted Other Class Suit No. 125 of 1991 in the court of the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Naogaon for declaration of title in the suit land, contending inter alia that the suit land originally belonged to Niroda Sundari and Dasya in equal share  Mrinalini Dasya orally relinquished her share in favour of Niroda Sundari who became the owner of 16 annas share in the suit land. On 23.6.1947 Niroda Sundari sold the same to one Haider Ali by a registered sale deed No. 3142. Thereafter Haider Ali sold the suit land to the plaintiff No. 1-2 through registered sale deed dated 29.8.1968 and handed over possession to them. to ignorance of Haider Ali thy land was wrongly recorded in the name of Niroda Sundari in S. A. Khatian. Since the Patnitola Sub-registrar's Office was burnt during war of liberation they could not obtain original copy of the sale deed and as such they have filed the certified copy of the aforesaid deed, which was obtained before war of liberation. During R. S. operation it was wrongly recorded in the name of the defendants along with the names of the plaintiffs and quantum of land in R.S. Plot No. 221 was recorded as 1.17 acres in place of 1.77 acres of land. The R.S. record was wrong.

 3. The defendant petitioners herein contested the suit by filing written statement denying material allegations made in the plaint, contending inter alia, that admittedly Niroda Sundari was the original owner of the suit land and the plain-tiffs' father and the father of the defendants were full brothers who purchased the suit land in the name of the plaintiffs and the defendants as well, in equal share and in R.S. Khatian the land was correctly recorded in their names.

4. The trial court decreed the suit. The defendant petitioners preferred Title Appeal No. 222 of 1993 before the learned District Judge, Naogaon challenging the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Naogaon which was heard, on transfer, by the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Naogaon, who by the impugned judgment dated 30.4.1997 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment of the trial court. The petitioners preferred the instant Civil Revision against the impugned judgment and obtained the Rule. 

5. Mr. A.K.M. Asaduzzaman, the learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that the courts below without dis-cussing any evidence whatsoever decreed the suit. The trial court did not discuss any evidence and arrived at an erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice, inasmuch as the learned Assistant Judge failed to consider that the plaintiffs did not produce the original deed of their title, claimed to have been executed and registered in favour of them by Haider Ali. On the other hand the defendants claimed that the suit land originally belonged to Niroda Sundari from whom their father and the plaintiffs father jointly purchased the suit land in the name of the plaintiffs and themselves in equal share and there was no existence of any deed of transfer being executed and registered by Haider Ali. As the father of the plaintiff was the elder brother of the father of the defendants and he being clever person and Chairman of the local Union Parishad for more than 30 years, all the documents of their properties were kept in his custody. The plaintiffs in collusion with their father has suppressed the original deed and since the Patnitola Sub-registrar's Office was burnt during war of liberation they have created certified copy of the sale deed showing Haider Ali as the vendor of the sale deed but in fact there was no such deed. All the deeds filed by the plaintiffs in the trial court are forged and created for the purpose of the suit. He further submits that in R.S. record the suit land was recorded in the name of the plaintiffs and the defendants in equal share on the basis of title deeds and physical possession and they have shown the suit land in their respective statement filed to the Government in respect of ownership of the land. He further submits that the trial court did not all consider the evidence of the defendants. By oral evidence also the defendants were able to prove their right, title and possession in the suit land. The Appellate Court below has also committed the same mistake in not discussing any evidence and recording independent findings which is a violation of mandatory pro-vision of law i.e. Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and thus the judgments of both the courts below suffer from legal infirmities, such as misreading and non reading of evidence. The learned Advocate submits that in this circumstances the suit may be sent back on remand to the Appellate Court below for writing a proper judgment. In this regard he refers to the case reported in AIR. 1969 (Rajastan) 9. On careful reading of the aforesaid decision it appears that the same has no manner of application in the present case inasmuch as the said suit was sent back on remand as the court below wrongly excluded the statement of the plaintiff from evidence. 

6. He further submits that the courts below arrived at an erroneous decision that the plaintiffs have mutated their names, though no papers was filed in support of their contention. As per him the S.A. Khatian was finally published in the year 1965 and the deed of transfer in favour of Haider Ali alleged to have been registered on 23.6.1947 but Haider Ali did not take any steps to rectify the S.A. Khatian which was prepared and published in the name of Niroda Sundari.

 7. Mr. S. N. the learned Advocate for the opposite parties submits that the ownership of Niroda Sundari is admitted who sold the suit land to Haider Ali on 23.6.1947 and thereafter Haider Ali transferred the suit land on 29.8.1968 by registered deed in favour of the plaintiffs but wrongly the S.A. record was prepared in the name of Niroda Sundari in place of Haider Ali and after purchase they have paid rent to the Government and obtained rent receipts which were marked as exhibits in the trial court. On propel consideration of the oral and documentary evidence the learned Assistant Judge, Naogaon has decreed the suit. On appeal the Appellate Court below by the impugned judgment rightly affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

8. In reply to the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioners that the judgments of both the courts below suffer from legal infirmities since the same were passed without discussing any evidence, Mr. S. N. Goswami, the learned Advocate for the opposite party submits that although the courts below did not discuss the evidences in so many words but they have duly considered the evidences on record both oral and documentary and they have passed their respective judgments with reference to the evidences on record and arrived at a con-current finding, which cannot be disturbed by this court exercising the revisional jurisdiction under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his contention Mr. Goswami refers to decisions reported in 7 BLT (AD) 147 and also 5 BLT (AD) 219 on this point. Mr. Goswami further submits that if it is found that the courts below did not dis-cuss and consider the evidences on record properly this court can consider the same and can pass a proper judgment without sending the case on remand. In support of this submission he refers to a decision reported in 3 BLT (AD) 139 wherein it has been held that "It is not inconsonance with equity and justice that an old case of 30 years could be remanded so lightly by the High Court Division even if it is accepted there is misreading of evidence and non-consideration of material evidence then the High Court Division was within competence to dispose of the matter on the materials on record without remanding the suit".

 9. Heard the learned Advocates for the parties and perused the revisional application and evidence on record both oral and documentary and the judgments passed by both the courts below. It appears from the judgments of the trial court as well as the Appellate Court below that the learned Judges have considered and made reference to the documentary evidence but they did not discuss any oral evidence of either side and the Appellate Court below being final court of fact ought to have discussed and recorded his findings independently but it is unfortunate that the Appellate Court below passed the impugned judgment avoiding the mandatory provisions of law. In this circumstances and in light of the decisions cited from the Bar I am inclined to discuss and consider the evidences both oral and documentary, available in the case record and for the purpose of disposal of this Rule I propose to discuss the evidences precisely. 

10. It appears from the plaint that the plaintiffs claimed their title by purchase of the suit land from one Haider Ali, who purchased the same from Niroda Sundari and they have claimed that the R.S. record was wrong and in R.S. Plot No. 221 of Khatian No. 35, the quantum of land was recorded as 1.17 acres in place of 1.77 acres of land. It appears from the written statement filed by the Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 that they claimed their title through purchase from Niroda Sundari by their father and uncle, the father of the plain-tiffs, jointly. In paragraph No. 6 of their written statement they have stated that their father died in the year 1964-65. In paragraph No. 9 of the written statement they have claimed that the deed of title of the plaintiffs was forged, which the Defendant No. 1 would prove at the time of trial and also prayed for impounding the certified copy of the sale deed, being filed by the plaintiff. In paragraph 14 of the written statement the defendants claimed that while their father and the father of the plaintiffs were in joint Mess they have purchased the suit land in the names of their respective sons from Niroda. Sundari in equal share. 

11. P.W. 1 Ashraful Hoque Chowdhury proved his title supporting the case as stated in the plaint. In cross-examination he has clearly stated that as the Patnitola Sub-registrar's Office was burnt during the war of liberation. They could not obtain the original copy of the deed of title but they obtained the certified copy of the sale deed earlier which was filed in the court from their custody and the same was marked as Exhibit 1(Ka). On perusal of exhibit 1(Ka) it appears that the certified copy of the sale deed was obtained on 31.1.1968. The sale deed of Niroda Sundari was marked as Exhibit 1, which was registered in the year 1947 and the same was admitted in evidence without formal proof as it was old document of over 30 years. Exhibit 2 is the D.C.R. in respect of Mutation Case No. 308 of 1979-80 in favour of the plaintiffs. Exhibit 3- 3(ka)-3(Cha) are the rent receipts obtained by the plaintiff and their father. Exhibit-3- 3(Ka)L3(Cha) prove that the father of the plaintiffs paid rent to the government some time in the name of Niroda Sundari and thereafter in the name of the plain-tiffs. Exhibit-6 is the certified copy of the notice of land transfer in respect of the sale deed being executed and registered by Haider Ali in favour of the plaintiffs. 

12. The defendants only filed copies of the statements of landed properties belonged to themselves and the plaintiffs, which were marked as Exhibit (Ka) and Ka(1) respectively. It appears from the cross-examination of D.W. 1 Abdus Sattar Chowdhury that their father and the father of the plaintiffs purchased the suit land from Niroda Sundari jointly. In cross-examination he stated that his father died in the year 1965 and he did not see the deed in question which was claimed to have been registered in favour of them by-Niroda Sundari and he also admitted that in the S.A. Plot No. 93 the land was 1.77 acres but it was wrongly recorded in R.S. record as 1.17 acres and he further admit-ted that Patnitola Sub-registrar's Office was burnt during war of liberation. The other P.Ws. only proved the possession of the plaintiffs and on the other hand the D.Ws. have proved the possession of the defendants in the suit land in their respective shares but on close scrutiny it is found that the P.Ws. are contiguous boundary men of the suit land, on the other hand the D.W. 2 and 3 are neither neighbours nor boundary men of the suit land. 

13. On due consideration of the documentary evidences on record in juxtaposition with the cross-examination of D.W. 1 it has been clearly proved that the claim of the defendants are down right false because the sale deed being executed and registered by Haider All was registered in favour of the plaintiffs on 29.1.1968 but admittedly the father of the defendants died in the year 1965. So the question of joint purchase by the father of the plaintiffs and the father of the defendants does not arise at all and this single fact falsify the claim of the defendants. The plaintiffs proved its case by producing both oral and documentary evidence. Exhibit 1 being supported by exhibit 6 being an age old document of over 30 years. It has presumptive value under Section 90 of the Evidence Act and the Exhibit 1(Ka), the certified copy of the original sale deed being admitted in evidence without objection in the trial court and as such no objection can be raised at this stage challenging the legality and propriety of the said certified copy of the sale deed. At the same time in the written statement the defendants have taken bur-den of proof that the certified copy of the sale deed, Exhibit I (Ka) as forged and fraudulent but the defendants failed to prove the same and as such the certified copy of an old document of over 30 years old having presumptive value under Section 90 of the Evidence Act and admissible in evidence. Exhibit 1(Ka) cannot be thrown out of consideration and rent receipts being filed by the plaintiffs are the collateral evidence of their possession being followed by title.

14. From the discussion made above it can be safely concluded that the plaintiffs were able to prove their title and possession in the suit land both by oral and documentary evidence. On the other hand, the defendants by their own evidence have disproved their case. 

15. Though the judgments passed by the courts below suffer from irregularity but the courts below committed no illegality or error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in arriving at a final decision and as such no interference is called for by this court upon the impugned judgment and decree. 

16. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost. 

17. Send down the lower courts record immediately.

End.
